task.question: Who wins the special election in Georgia in 2026?
task.evidence: Assistant District Attorney Clay Fuller, a Trump-endorsed Republican, wins the special election in Georgia to replace Marjorie Taylor Greene, who resigned in January following a public fallout with Trump.

answer:
Based on the search results, in the special election for Georgia's 14th Congressional District in 2026, **Clay Fuller** (Republican) won the runoff election on April 7, 2026. Fuller, a former district attorney, defeated Democrat Shawn Harris, a retired Army brigadier general.

FINAL: Clay Fuller (Republican) won the Georgia 14th Congressional District special election in 2026.

        As no candidate received more than 50% of the vote, a runoff election between district attorney Clay Fuller and cattleman Shawn Harris was held on April 7, 2026, [2] with Fuller winning to serve the remainder of the 119th United States Congress, ending January 3, 2027. Election Results Clayton Fuller (R) defeated Shawn Harris (D) in a special runoff election to represent Georgia's 14th Congressional District on April 7, 2026. Neither received a majority of votes in a special election on March 10, 2026, with Harris receiving 37.3% of the vote and Fuller 34.9%. Republican Clay Fuller, a former district attorney, defeated Democrat Shawn Harris, a retired Army brigadier general, in a special election to replace former GOP Rep. Marjorie Taylor Greene.
